sources.note: Mostly Vaibhav on streaming and BAML; Dex speaks on design points, tool-call streaming, static HTML, unidirectional data flow, contracts.

sources.title: AI That Works #53 Agentic Coding for Frontend Apps
AI That Works #54 Harness Engineering Without the Hype
sources.note: README and meta only (no transcript given). Highlight quotes are not individually attributed to Dex; guests include Viv (LangChain) and the Ralph loop creator.

cards.source_title: AI That Works #53 Agentic Coding for Frontend Apps
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you find out your unknowns during planning instead of during implementation
cards.claim: Extend learning tests to UX unknowns: build throwaway pure components in Storybook before the plan, because a plan document cannot tell you whether a UI will look good.
cards.evidence_detail: Describes HumanLayer's own practice; the tips-to-modals feature had plan docs he could not judge visually.
cards.landing: Phase routine pre-plan step: a cheap proof script or stub that resolves an unknown before the plan is written

cards.source_title: AI That Works #53 Agentic Coding for Frontend Apps
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you can't read the plan and know whether it's going to look good
cards.claim: Frontend work needs a different workflow from backend: for backend, reading the plan is enough to judge it, for frontend you have to see it, so heavy up-front markdown planning is a poor fit.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated as the motivation for the episode; no measurements.
cards.landing: Phase routine: declare which phases need a visible artifact before plan approval (web manager UI phases)

cards.source_title: AI That Works #53 Agentic Coding for Frontend Apps
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you don't need a plan to build one pure component
cards.claim: Do not plan small, visually judged pieces: build the pure component family from an outline, riff on its states, and only then write the plan for the multi-system wiring.
cards.evidence_detail: His own workflow; plan only for work spanning four systems across two repos.
cards.landing: Phase routine: a lighter path for small UI phases versus the full plan-first path

cards.source_title: AI That Works #53 Agentic Coding for Frontend Apps
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: unit testing for visual stuff
cards.claim: Storybook is unit testing for UI: reproduce a bad state by setting props rather than clicking through a running app to recreate it.
cards.evidence_detail: Example: a to-do card wrong in 'deleting' state fixed by editing props in a story; 'every bug adds a story' is how their Storybook grew.
cards.landing: Web manager (src/): Storybook or a props-driven state gallery as a fast verifier for UI bugs

cards.source_title: AI That Works #53 Agentic Coding for Frontend Apps
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you have pure components that just take props and render
cards.claim: Split pure render-only components from wired components that fetch and hold state; only pure ones go in Storybook and the agent reasons about one thing at a time.
cards.evidence_detail: Architecture rule; HumanLayer keeps pure ones in packages/ui shared by apps; Riptide has a story per coding-agent output type.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md or src/ conventions: pure vs wired component rule; smaller per-task context

cards.source_title: AI That Works #53 Agentic Coding for Frontend Apps
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: make sure it's actually importing your shared components
cards.claim: Failure mode: Claude draws a duplicate component inside Storybook instead of importing the real one, so the story never exercises the app; check the story imports the shared component.
cards.evidence_detail: Seen repeatedly by him; he checked the generated stories file during the demo.
cards.landing: Reviewer checklist item: verify the test or story imports the production code under test, not a copy

cards.source_title: AI That Works #53 Agentic Coding for Frontend Apps
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Claude understands this concept of pure versus wired. It's not super baked in the training set
cards.claim: The model does not know the pure/wired pattern by default, so it must be stated in the prompt or instructions.
cards.evidence_detail: His experience; 'if you prompt it properly, you can get there'.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md / skill: a short pattern rule for the web app

cards.source_title: AI That Works #53 Agentic Coding for Frontend Apps
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: I just use agent browser basically
cards.claim: Close the visual loop with a browser-agent skill that screenshots the story and feeds the PNG back to the model; no human for pure visual changes.
cards.evidence_detail: Uses Vercel's agent-browser skill; fell back to the browser agent shipped in gstack.
cards.landing: .claude/skills/: a screenshot/browser verification skill for the web manager

cards.source_title: AI That Works #53 Agentic Coding for Frontend Apps
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: maybe we need a skill for like setting up storybook and extracting styles
cards.claim: Bootstrap friction (styles, theming) is a candidate for a reusable skill; he bootstrapped faster by pointing the agent at an existing Storybook as a starter template.
cards.evidence_detail: Five components in about five minutes by copying another repo's Storybook.
cards.landing: Skills: setup recipes captured from a working example rather than rewritten each time

cards.source_title: AI That Works #53 Agentic Coding for Frontend Apps
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: This is why we do plan mode.
cards.claim: Reading the plan catches stale-knowledge errors: the default plan picked Storybook 8 and he knew 10 was current; Crispy would have web-searched the latest version.
cards.evidence_detail: Observed live in Vaibhav's repo; same issue with an old Rust crate version in the plan.
cards.landing: Plan/research step: check dependency versions against the web, not the model's memory

cards.source_title: AI That Works #53 Agentic Coding for Frontend Apps
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Always read, you have to read the plans. You should read something.
cards.claim: A human must read the plan even when little else is read.
cards.evidence_detail: Said while reviewing Vaibhav's plan.
cards.landing: Phase routine: owner view/plan review checkpoint

cards.source_title: AI That Works #53 Agentic Coding for Frontend Apps
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you could do it incrementally
cards.claim: Migrate a brownfield repo to a new pattern one component at a time with a small scoped prompt, not an all-at-once migration.
cards.evidence_detail: Advice during a live migration; the prompt asked for a single, already-pure component.
cards.landing: Phase sizing: one small slice per phase, bootstrap then add one

cards.source_title: AI That Works #53 Agentic Coding for Frontend Apps
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: find a way to move things out of Figma earlier and earlier
cards.claim: Agents are good at code in distribution and poor at WYSIWYG tools or MCP into them, so make mockups be the real components and drop the translation step.
cards.evidence_detail: Teams moving fastest do this; his designer 'hates Figma now'; no numbers.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious (design handoff for the web manager)

cards.source_title: AI That Works #53 Agentic Coding for Frontend Apps
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: if you're not willing to migrate to a monorepo
cards.claim: Second-hand claim: agent-tool vendors refuse enterprise clients unwilling to move to a monorepo because agent results are much better there.
cards.evidence_detail: Reported from unnamed people who build coding agent tools.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious (FixFlow is already a single monorepo)

cards.source_title: AI That Works #53 Agentic Coding for Frontend Apps
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: it's only as good as the data set that you create
cards.claim: Snapshot tests are brittle and only as good as the cases captured, so every production failure should be turned into a new snapshot case; he prefers visual checking for now.
cards.evidence_detail: Answer to an audience question.
cards.landing: CI/regression policy: each production bug adds a fixture or regression test

cards.source_title: AI That Works #53 Agentic Coding for Frontend Apps
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Kyle wanted to integrate this charting library
cards.claim: Get a new library working in isolation first (in Storybook) before wiring it, as a learning test.
cards.evidence_detail: Kyle's charting library for dashboards; 'once baked, it just works everywhere'.
cards.landing: Phase routine: spike new dependencies in isolation before the plan

cards.source_title: AI That Works #53 Agentic Coding for Frontend Apps
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: we will as a team review just the storybook stuff
cards.claim: Review the design artifact on its own in PR review: pull down and look at only the components.
cards.evidence_detail: Team practice at HumanLayer.
cards.landing: Reviewer step for UI PRs: inspect the rendered artifact, not only the diff

cards.source_title: AI That Works #53 Agentic Coding for Frontend Apps
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you can freeform and jump straight to structure outline skill
cards.claim: Use a lighter path for small tasks: freeform, then a structure-outline skill as a mini plan, rather than the full Crispy flow, which takes 15 to 20 minutes.
cards.evidence_detail: Vaibhav says full Crispy plan mode takes 15-20 minutes; Dex suggests the mini plan.
cards.landing: Phase routine: a tiered path (full plan versus mini outline) by task size

cards.source_title: AI That Works #53 Agentic Coding for Frontend Apps
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: your options are either get your AI to write Stitch or Figma or Canva
cards.claim: Prefer working where the model is in distribution (React code on disk) over tools reached through MCP.
cards.evidence_detail: Argument for Storybook over Figma MCP.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious

cards.source_title: AI That Works #52 SSE Streaming
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: your bar for creating an XJS app or a VEAT app should be significantly higher
cards.claim: Start with a static HTML file plus JavaScript before adopting a framework, since the agent can write it quickly and convert it later; this lowers early-prototype cost.
cards.evidence_detail: One of his 'new favorite tactics'; used to demo the streaming endpoint.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious (small internal tools or evidence viewers)

cards.source_title: AI That Works #52 SSE Streaming
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: What about the system allowed them to break something
cards.claim: When a change breaks something with no failing test, ask why a contract, type or pre-merge check did not enforce the dependency; fix the system, not the person.
cards.evidence_detail: Said in reply to a question on code breaking dependents; no example.
cards.landing: CI import-boundary contracts; post-incident rule: every escape yields a new check

cards.source_title: AI That Works #52 SSE Streaming
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: unidirectional data flow where all writes go to an API server
cards.claim: Riptide uses one-way data flow: all writes go to the API and the database, and database changes stream to subscribed clients; cancellation propagates down to the source request.
cards.evidence_detail: Brief description of Riptide architecture.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious

cards.source_title: AI That Works #52 SSE Streaming
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: It only streams when the JSON block is finished.
cards.claim: Claude Code streams per turn and per finished tool call, not per token, while Codex streams every token; the Agent SDK does not stream bash output, so progress cannot be shown.
cards.evidence_detail: Observed behaviour discussed during the whiteboard section.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious (relevant to any monitoring of long workflow runs)

cards.source_title: AI That Works #52 SSE Streaming
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: I'm gonna write you a script that provisions an API key with a $3 budget
cards.claim: Give a demo or experiment its own API key with a hard dollar cap.
cards.evidence_detail: Offered as a joke-adjacent aside in the live build; no further detail.
cards.landing: Workflow runs: budget-capped keys per experiment

cards.source_title: AI That Works #54 Harness Engineering Without the Hype
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: exhaust all the avenues in the single-while-loop stack
cards.claim: Exhaust the single agent loop before adding a second loop, and fix the instruction set with your team rather than throwing more compute at it (speaker not individually attributed in the README).
cards.evidence_detail: README highlight quote; README only.
cards.landing: Workflow-tool orchestration: justify each added agent layer

cards.source_title: AI That Works #54 Harness Engineering Without the Hype
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Look at the damn data.
cards.claim: Inspect what comes back instead of telling the model to figure it out; people never look at the returned data (speaker not individually attributed).
cards.evidence_detail: README highlight quote; README only.
cards.landing: Evidence folders: reviewers read raw outputs, not summaries

cards.source_title: AI That Works #54 Harness Engineering Without the Hype
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: The evals are what survive.
cards.claim: Code written around a model release may go stale, but a production-grounded eval set outlives models and harnesses; beware overfitting if the generated prompt looks like 60 if-else cases (speaker not individually attributed).
cards.evidence_detail: README highlight and takeaway; README only.
cards.landing: Knowledge-store pilot: cold-resume trial as a durable eval

cards.source_title: AI That Works #54 Harness Engineering Without the Hype
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Only build your own harness if you're going to RL a model
cards.claim: Building your own harness only pays when training a model on your tools; otherwise you compete with a 40-50 person team improving the stock harness (speaker not individually attributed).
cards.evidence_detail: README takeaway; README only.
cards.landing: Reinforces using Claude Code's built-in hooks, skills and agents rather than a custom harness

gaps: 2026-04-21 Harness Engineering episode: no transcript supplied, only README and meta; its highlight quotes are not attributed to a speaker, so author Dex is a guess.
SSE episode is largely Vaibhav-led (BAML streaming attributes, asyncio semaphore); those were not carded as Dex's.
Dex's SSE lines are auto-captions of only one side; the Vaibhav replies were not read, so context for some Dex remarks is thin.
